evidence: The required end-to-end demonstration reaches an explicit contract, not an additional snapshot guarantee. In Visibility across chunks the spec requires every level-0 worker to receive classified entries from earlier messages even before their blocks are stored, and permits concurrent workers; in Deterministic record and transition contract it says query/request start Open, accept Resolved, and submit validation checks status validity. That same section expressly requires reconstructing fetched bundles using fetched_at 'to keep submit validation stable across other workers’ arrivals.' Consider a query i.12 and two later chunks A and B containing answer messages 20 and 27 respectively. Fetch B while A is unstored: cumulative deterministic prefill gives B the Open i.12, so B can propose Resolved citing its own message 27 (the spec requires cites in the current chunk and strictly after the source). Now A commits a structurally valid resolution citing 20 after B's fetch, but with created_at equal to B's fetched_at. On B's submit, a timestamp-only reconstruction includes A, applies its stored transition after seeding the deterministic source, and reconstructs i.12 as Resolved rather than Open. B's originally valid resolution is rejected because the target is now closed. This directly violates the promised stable submit validation across other workers' arrivals, even though the final ledger may already be resolved by A. This is not the explicitly excluded model-discovered-work limit: i.12 is a classified deterministic source already supplied to B. The named spec provides no captured membership or commit-order tie boundary and does not accept timestamp collisions as a tradeoff. Read-only context verifies the inherited machinery really uses this unsafe boundary: src/store/summary.rs load_level0_records selects created_at<=fetched_at (lines 574-590); bundle_fold passes fetched_at to that selector (1181); summary fetch stores now.0 as fetched_at (1334-1346); insert_block stores now.0 as created_at (1384-1404); summary_submit rebuilds the bundle (1547). src/summary/validate.rs rejects a transition target whose folded status is closed (167-174). No existing exclusion of a later equal-timestamp commit appears in those snapshot rules. Fixing or explicitly validating this inherited assumption is material to the new design's stated stability contract; the proposed frozen-clock reconstruction test is a suitable focused check.
